With no tab to preview over (an empty Space), a click opens the page in a new tab

AR-10.note: ⌘Y (Ctrl+H), Archive → View History (macOS) and the command bar open History, a Library section next to the Archive (not a page in a tab): every visit of the current profile from the history store, newest first by day, virtualised and paged, with search (all words, title or address). A row opens its page in a new tab (⌘-click or middle-click: behind the Library); its × or its menu (Open in New Tab, Open in Background, Copy Link, Remove from History) removes every visit to the page. Clearing the Archive leaves it alone

AR-11.note: Backups of the whole sidebar (Spaces, each profile’s Favorites, pinned and Today tabs, folders, split views; no private profiles) in userData/backups, one JSON file each: taken within 5 minutes of a sidebar change (only when it differs from the newest; browsing alone never makes one), once 30 s after launch, before every restore, and with Back Up Now. Kept: the newest 10 of today, then the newest of each of the 10 days before, of each week of the month before that and of each 30 days of the year before that. Help → Restore Data… (macOS) and the command bar open the Backups section of the Library: a dated list (day headings, time, Spaces and tabs); Restore… asks first, then puts the sidebar back in one step: tabs in both keep their page, tabs only in the backup come back asleep (with the page and history the Archive kept for them, leaving the Archive), tabs opened since go to the Archive, Spaces added since go. The toast’s Undo and ⌘Z restore the backup taken just before
